original_native_abi.calling_convention: x86-32 thiscall, receiver in ECX, one 32-bit type word on the stack at [ESP+0x4]
original_native_abi.return_semantics: EAX holds the sub-object pointer for the requested ObjectTYPE word, or 0; the third path tail-jumps to 0x00950eb0 which also returns a pointer in EAX
original_native_abi.return_type_rationale: The SDK FUNCTION_DEF for /Spore/UTFWin/PerspectiveEffect::func80h declares RETURN_TYPE void, but that entry is the SDK's generated placeholder for the unnamed vftable slot 0x80. The authoritative declaration for the slot this code occupies is /Spore/Object::Cast in the same XML: RETURN_TYPE 'void *', CONVENTION thiscall, parameters (Object *this, ObjectTYPE typeID), and Object__vftable names that slot Cast at OFFSET 0xc. The machine agrees with Cast: every path materialises EAX (0x009804f8 LEA EAX,[ECX+0xc], 0x009804fe XOR EAX,EAX) and the fallback path tail-jumps into a function whose EAX is a pointer. Modelled as void* and recorded as PARTIAL on this single point.

vtable_dispatch_semantics: The three references above are all inbound: 0x014440dc names this function as a vftable entry and the two thunks jump to it. This function dispatches nothing itself - the body is a compare against 0xef2b293b, a null-receiver test, an LEA forming self+0xc, and a direct tail jump to 0x00950eb0. The vtable shapes in the header describe the object's layout, not a dispatch site of this function.
observed_mechanics: 0x009804e0 MOV EAX,[ESP+0x4] then 0x009804e4 CMP EAX,0xef2b293b: the stack dword is the ObjectTYPE word and the receiver stays in ECX. Ghidra's decompilation shows the operands swapped only because it typed the function with an unknown calling convention.

0xef2b293b is ENUM_ENTRY 'UTFWin::IPerspectiveEffect' in the Spore SDK ObjectTYPE enum (also duplicated onto UTFWin::IGlideEffect and UTFWin::IRotateEffect, which is why Ghidra warns that some enum values lack unique names).
On 0xef2b293b: 0x009804f4 TEST ECX,ECX / JZ 0x009804fe, then 0x009804f8 LEA EAX,[ECX+0xc]; a null receiver yields 0x009804fe XOR EAX,EAX. So the result is the sub-object at object+0x0c, or null.

Any other type word: 0x009804eb MOV [ESP+0x4],EAX (a redundant re-spill of the same value) then 0x009804ef JMP 0x00950eb0 - a tail call that leaves ECX and the stack argument untouched, so the receiver and the type word are forwarded unchanged.

0x00950eb0 is the same virtual slot in the base class: 0x2f009dd0 ('UTFWin::IWinProc') returns the object itself, 0xee3f516e ('Object') and 0xeec58382 ('UTFWin::ILayoutElement') return object+4, everything else returns 0. It occupies ~20 vftables in SporeApp.exe and has nine direct call sites.
Two this-adjusting thunks jump to the target: 0x00980660 'SUB ECX,4 / JMP 0x009804e0' and 0x00980670 'SUB ECX,0xc / JMP 0x009804e0'.

0x00980660 is the Cast slot of the vftable 0x014440b4 that the constructor stores at object+0x04, and 0x00980670 is the Cast slot of the vftable 0x01444098 stored at object+0x0c, so casting to 0xef2b293b hands back a sub-object whose own Cast slot re-enters this function with the receiver adjusted back down by 0x0c.

Constructor at 0x00980680 requests 0x14 bytes from 0x009512d0 and initialises [+0x00]=0x014440d0, [+0x04]=0x014440b4, [+0x08]=0, [+0x0c]=0x01444098; the +0x08 dword is not reachable through any ObjectTYPE word in either implementation.

The shape is a per-class family: sibling override 0x0097e7f0 has the same 'compare, else tail-call the base' body with its own word 0xcf3df10b ('UTFWin::ILayoutStyle') returning self+0x0c, and the reconstructed re_0095f960 / re_00957510 in PKG-UTFWIN-CORE-WAVE6 use the same words.
No globals are read or written and the function is not gated on any runtime state: every input is either the receiver or the type word.
